```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
from plotnine import options

import ezrsurvey as ez

options.figure_size = (9, 5)
options.dpi = 150

survey = ez.podracing_survey
ez.use_dataset(survey)

# Every figure quoted in the prose is computed here and interpolated inline, so
# the narrative cannot drift away from the charts when the data changes.
n_total = len(survey)
nps = int(ez.calc_nps("nps_value")["nps"].iloc[0])
groups = ez.nps_group(survey["nps_value"]).astype(float)
share_promoter = round((groups == 1).mean() * 100)
share_detractor = round((groups == -1).mean() * 100)

ipm = ez.ipm_model("nps_value", "ratings_")
threshold = ez.bands_rating_3()["to"].iloc[0]
priority = ipm[ipm["performance"] < threshold].sort_values("importance", ascending=False)
strongest = ipm.sort_values("performance", ascending=False).iloc[0]
top_driver = ipm.sort_values("importance", ascending=False).iloc[0]

regions = ez.calc_nps("nps_value", by="region").sort_values("nps", ascending=False)
best_region = regions.iloc[0]
worst_region = regions.iloc[-1]

motivations = ez.calc_percentage_multi("motivations_", id="respondent_id", sort="desc")
gender = ez.calc_percentage("demo_gender", sort="desc")
mean_age = ez.calc_summary("demo_age")["mean"].iloc[0]

returning = ez.calc_percentage("satis_return")
share_return = round(returning.loc[returning["satis_return"].isin(["Likely", "Very likely"]), "pct"].sum())

priority_list = ", ".join(f"{row.feature} ({row.performance:.2f})" for row in priority.itertuples())
```

A study of `{python} f"{n_total:,}"` pod-racing fans, covering how they rate
the experience, what drives their willingness to recommend it, and where the
opportunities sit. Code is shown alongside the output so the analysis can be
audited and re-run; for a blank scaffold to start your own report from, use
`ez.scaffold_report()`.

## Executive summary

The fan base recommends pod racing, but narrowly. The Net Promoter Score is
**`{python} f"{nps:+d}"`** on a base of `{python} f"{n_total:,}"`:
`{python} share_promoter`% promoters against `{python} share_detractor`%
detractors, with `{python} share_return`% saying they are likely to return next
season. This is not a lukewarm crowd so much as a divided one, and the division
is explainable.

Enthusiasm rests on the spectacle. `{python} round(motivations["pct"].iloc[0])`%
attend for the `{python} str(motivations["option"].iloc[0])`, and
`{python} strongest["feature"]` is the best-delivered part of the experience at
`{python} f"{strongest['performance']:.2f}"` out of 5. That is the asset to
protect.

What holds the score down is delivery on the basics.
`{python} len(priority)` of the `{python} len(ipm)` rated features fall below
the acceptable threshold of `{python} f"{threshold:.1f}"`: `{python} priority_list`.
The most consequential of these is **`{python} priority["feature"].iloc[0]`**,
which carries `{python} round(priority["importance"].iloc[0])`% of explained
importance in the recommendation model while being rated only
`{python} f"{priority['performance'].iloc[0]:.2f}"`. It is the highest-return
fix available.

The weakness is also regional rather than universal:
`{python} best_region["region"]` returns `{python} f"{int(best_region['nps']):+d}"`
against `{python} worst_region["region"]` at `{python} f"{int(worst_region['nps']):+d}"`,
a spread of `{python} int(best_region["nps"] - worst_region["nps"])` points that
no single global programme will close.

## The headline: willingness to recommend

`{python} f"{nps:+d}"` places the fan base in positive territory, but well
short of the enthusiasm the sport's own marketing assumes.

```{python}
ez.plot_nps_gauge(nps)
```

The distribution matters more than the single number. A score of
`{python} f"{nps:+d}"` could describe a uniformly tepid audience or a split
one; here it is the latter, with substantial mass at both ends.

```{python}
ez.plot_nps("nps_value")
```

Stated return intent corroborates it: `{python} share_return`% likely or very
likely to come back, with a sizeable undecided middle that is winnable.

```{python}
ez.calc_percentage("satis_return", sort="desc").pipe(ez.plot_bars)
```

### Where the score differs

```{python}
regions
```

`{python} best_region["region"]` leads on advocacy at
`{python} f"{int(best_region['nps']):+d}"`; `{python} worst_region["region"]`
trails at `{python} f"{int(worst_region['nps']):+d}"`. Read the bases in the
table before acting on any one region: the smaller cells carry margins of error
wide enough to overlap (see [Methodology](#methodology-and-precision)).

## What drives the score

`ez.ipm_model()` regresses recommendation on the rating block and crosses
importance against delivered performance. The quadrant to act on is upper
left: features that matter and are not being delivered.

```{python}
ez.plot_ipm(ipm)
```

`{python} top_driver["feature"]` carries the most weight in the model at
`{python} round(top_driver["importance"])`% of explained importance. Points are
coloured by the decision band they fall in, so anything sitting in the red zone
is below the acceptable threshold regardless of how close it looks to the next
band.

The full ranking:

```{python}
ipm.sort_values("importance", ascending=False)
```

Feature-level ratings show the same picture in distribution form, ordered by
weighted mean:

```{python}
ez.plot_rating_grid("ratings_")
```

### Movement against a benchmark

With a previous wave, `ez.compare_values()` and `ez.plot_diff()` show the
shift. Here the mechanics are illustrated against the scale midpoint, which
doubles as a read on how far each feature sits from acceptable:

```{python}
ez.compare_values(
    current=ipm[["feature", "performance"]],
    previous=ipm[["feature"]].assign(performance=threshold),
).pipe(ez.plot_diff)
```

## Who the audience is

`{python} round(gender["pct"].iloc[0])`% of respondents are
`{python} str(gender["demo_gender"].iloc[0]).lower()`, average age
`{python} round(mean_age)`.

```{python}
ez.calc_percentage("demo_gender", sort="desc").pipe(ez.plot_bars)
```

Occupation spreads across many long labels, so the chart switches itself to
horizontal bars:

```{python}
ez.calc_percentage("demo_job", sort="asc").pipe(ez.plot_bars)
```

Motivations are a check-all-that-apply block, counted over respondents rather
than ticks, so the percentages intentionally sum past 100:

```{python}
motivations.pipe(ez.plot_bars, label="option")
```

`{python} round(motivations["pct"].iloc[0])`% come for the
`{python} str(motivations["option"].iloc[0])`, ahead of
`{python} str(motivations["option"].iloc[1])` at
`{python} round(motivations["pct"].iloc[1])`%.
`{python} str(motivations["option"].iloc[-1])` is the minority motive, which
bears on how heavily that category should front the sponsorship mix.

A crosstab turns any pair of questions into a report-ready table:

```{python}
ez.crosstab("region", "demo_gender", cell="row_pct")
```

## In their own words

`ez.sample_comments_diverse()` selects maximally different verbatims. These are
illustrative of the range of opinion, not a measurement of how common each view
is.

```{python}
ez.sample_comments_diverse("nps_com", "show_com", n=8, seed=42).pipe(ez.plot_quotes_tree)
```

## Weighting the sample

The achieved sample is `{python} round(gender["pct"].iloc[0])`%
`{python} str(gender["demo_gender"].iloc[0]).lower()`. Where the fan population
is known to differ, `ez.set_weights()` rakes the sample to the targets and
every summary helper picks the weights up automatically, reporting `wpct`
beside the unweighted `pct`:

```{python}
ez.set_weights({"variable": "demo_gender", "Male": 0.49, "Female": 0.50, "Non-binary": 0.01})
weighted = ez.calc_percentage("satis_return", sort="desc")
ez.clear_weights()
weighted
```

## Methodology and precision {#methodology-and-precision}

`{python} f"{n_total:,}"` responses. `ez.precision_summary()` reports the margin
of error each headline figure carries; quote it whenever two percentages are
compared, because differences smaller than the margin are not differences.

```{python}
ez.precision_summary("demo_gender", ez.starts_with("ratings_"))
```
